web.help.start.title: Start your first broadcast
web.help.start.summary: Sign in, prepare the room, connect OBS, then confirm going live.
web.help.start.body:
1. Open Accounts, scan the QR code with the Bilibili mobile app, and approve sign-in. If the QR code is unavailable, copy the link and open it in your phone's browser to verify; verification cannot be completed in a desktop browser. If copying fails, copy manually from the displayed link field. Your room loads automatically; if it does not appear, return to Studio and refresh the room.

2. Check the title and category in Studio. Edit ordinary settings in place. Fields with a Save button take effect after saving.

3. Enable the WebSocket server in OBS, enter its address and password, and connect. With automatic streaming enabled, going live configures OBS and starts its stream.

4. Choose Start live and review the confirmation. Check the operation result and live state; an accepted request is not a confirmed success.

Stopping also requires confirmation. Closing the browser does not stop the broadcast or quit the application. Press Ctrl+C in the launch window to run your configured live, OBS, and helper cleanup.
web.help.obs.title: Connect OBS and automate streaming
web.help.obs.summary: Understand the address, password, auto-connect, and automatic streaming.
web.help.obs.body:
Enable the server under Tools → WebSocket Server Settings in OBS. A common address is ws://127.0.0.1:4455; use the actual port configured in OBS. Save the matching address and password in the panel, then connect.

Auto-connect attempts to connect at application startup or when going live needs a connection. Automatic streaming starts OBS after live stream information has been obtained; disabling it prevents OBS from starting automatically.

Changing the address or password disconnects the current connection. Connect again afterward. Saved passwords are never filled into the browser; submitting an empty password clears the saved password.

Connected means the control channel is available, not that OBS is streaming. Read operation results when starting, stopping, or exiting; a failed stop is not reported as a successful stop.
web.help.room.title: Edit your live room
web.help.room.summary: Title, category, announcement, cover, and stream delay.
web.help.room.body:
Check the active account at the top of the page first. Edit the title and announcement directly in Studio, then save. The room updates only after saving succeeds.

Search category names and choose a specific category. You cannot go live without a category.

Choose or drop a PNG/JPEG in the browser, up to 12 MiB, 24 megapixels, and 16384 pixels per side. Drag the preview, use arrow keys, or adjust the sliders to position and zoom the crop. Reset restores the centered crop. Output matches Bilibili's current cover editor at 720×540 (4:3). Bilibili Web may display a 16:9 crop; keep important content near the center.

Preview cover sends the crop to the Arcana World backend, which compresses it to a JPEG up to 256 KiB and flattens transparency onto white. The confirmation shows the actual upload image and size; only final confirmation uploads it to Bilibili. Cancel returns to editing with the crop preserved. Closing the editor or switching accounts clears the draft. Successful upload does not mean platform review has completed.

Delay settings first load the platform's current value, then accept a nonnegative integer. Account permissions or platform restrictions may prevent an update; failures remain visible in the result and log.
web.help.chat.title: Chat and user management
web.help.chat.summary: Send messages, view Audience and Fleet lists, and manage moderators, blocked users, and mutes.
web.help.chat.body:
Prepare your room and OBS in Studio, then read and send messages in Chat. Messages may contain up to 40 characters. Enter sends; Shift+Enter adds a line break. Submitting clears the input; check the send result. Leaving the page discards unsubmitted input.

Pause updates to hold the displayed messages while receiving continues in the background. Resume shows current messages; Latest messages returns to the bottom. Switching pages does not stop listening.

Right-click a message or choose Actions to copy its text or UID, view the sender, open their homepage, mute, block, or appoint them as a moderator. With the Actions button focused, Shift+F10 opens the menu and Esc closes it. Mystery users and system messages without a valid identity have no user-management actions.

Audience and Fleet each show the top 20 members and support refresh. Moderators, Blacklist, and Muted users let you view existing lists, search by name or UID, and add or remove entries. Lists, profiles, and management forms open in dialogs. Mutes accept positive whole hours or a permanent duration. Changes require confirmation. Blocking removes the relationship with that user and restricts messaging, gifts, and other interactions.

Confirmation dialogs show only Cancel and the named action. Before submitting, Cancel or Esc returns to the user profile, list, or duration selection. Back discards unsubmitted search and duration input. Outside confirmation, Close or Esc exits management and returns focus to the action entry point.

Settings controls listening, the message limit, and additional events. Messages missed while the application was offline are not fetched later. History search remains in the terminal interface. The interface language does not translate audience messages.
web.help.outputs.title: Configure overlay and speech
web.help.outputs.summary: Choose output locations, appearance, voices, and received events.
web.help.outputs.body:
Outputs configures the chat overlay and speech separately. Both run on the computer hosting Arcana World, not on another device viewing the browser panel.

For the overlay, choose displays, position, typography, colors, and opacity. Check the result on the studio computer; actual content comes from received live events.

For speech, select a voice and volume, then preview to check audio output. Stop speech interrupts the current message and clears the queue. Disable speech to prevent subsequent messages too.

Overlay and speech have separate event selections. Enabling speech reads new events, not past messages. Missing helpers produce an error without preventing use of the other features.
web.help.privacy.title: Panel access and account safety
web.help.privacy.summary: Local access, account switching, and exit behavior.
web.help.privacy.body:
The main application uses your saved default interface, or the terminal interface if none is set. On Windows, run arcana-world-webui.exe beside the main executable to open WebUI directly. See --help for commands to save the default or select an interface for one run.

WebUI opens the default browser on startup. If opening fails, visit the address printed in the terminal. The server binds to 127.0.0.1 by default, at http://127.0.0.1:5273; use the port you specified if different. No access token is required, and the same address works after a restart.

If you manually expose the server beyond loopback, any device that can reach the port can control the stream. Restrict network access yourself. Closing the browser does not stop the server; press Ctrl+C in the terminal running the application to quit.

The browser never receives login cookies or saved OBS passwords. Stream keys are displayed only when explicitly requested.

Before switching or deleting the active account, the application checks and cleans up the old account's live state. Review the confirmation for its effect. Do not repeat commands while an identity change is running.

Command-line overrides apply only to the current run and disable the corresponding fields. The browser theme is saved separately in this browser and does not change the terminal theme.
web.help.troubleshooting.title: Troubleshoot connections and operations
web.help.troubleshooting.summary: Panel disconnects, OBS failures, missing chat, and helper errors.
web.help.troubleshooting.body:
Failed operations show a notification in the top-right corner. Expand Error details for longer messages, then dismiss the notification when finished.

Panel disconnected: confirm that Arcana World's Web server is running, check the address and port, then choose Reconnect. Last known state is not live state.

OBS connection failed: check that its WebSocket server is enabled and that the address, port, and password match. Reconnect after changing connection settings.

No chat or speech: check the active account, room, listening switch, and each output's event selection. Speech synthesis needs network access; audio and overlay output also need their corresponding helpers.

Setting unavailable: check whether a startup option overrides it or an operation is in progress. Read the result before repeatedly starting a stream or sending another message.

Open the log in Settings for details. Clearing application data deletes accounts, settings, history, and logs and then exits; do not use it as the first troubleshooting step.
